claims.rule: Match exported algebra strength to operational semantics; right-biased map union must not be promoted to a commutative semilattice merely because set union supports one.
claims.applicability: Historical NonEmptyMap review, 2018. For a current version, inspect collision semantics and registered laws before applying; this is not a general ban on Semilattice instances.
claims.counterexample: A coherent set union may be commutative and idempotent; weakening that instance solely to match map behavior would be a false positive.

claims.rule: For a new derived Functor operation, add an equivalence law to the existing primitive specification and register it without casually changing published discipline signatures.
claims.applicability: PR 4582 in 2024 and PR 4352 in 2022 support checking law APIs as published contracts. A,A registration leaves widening syntax to a distinct compile-time probe; no such probe ran here.
claims.counterexample: Repeating the same property separately for List, Option and Map is not automatically stronger than shared laws; widening syntax still needs a separate test rather than being declared covered by A,A.

claims.rule: Keep an encoding or instance-construction helper out of the public implicit API unless a concrete supported abstraction and compatibility plan justify exposing it.
claims.applicability: Observed Newtype decision in 2018 and NonEmptyReducible discussion in 2020, corroborated by contextual-only helper-scope discussion in PR 3962 in 2021. Preserve already-public contracts; documentation may be safer than retroactive privacy. No adopted StackSafeMonad/Defer change is inferred.
claims.counterexample: A deliberately documented public typeclass with consumers is not an internal helper just because its implementation is short or privately implemented.
